topics.name: Arrays & Strings

questions.prompt: Which data structure is most optimal to check for balanced brackets or parentheses in O(N) time?
questions.explanation: A Stack follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO), which matches the nesting order of opening and closing brackets.

questions.prompt: In Floyd’s Cycle-Finding algorithm (tortoise and hare), how do the two pointers traverse a linked list?
options: Both advance 1 node at a time
Slow advances 1 node, fast advances 2 nodes
Fast advances from end to start
Slow advances 2 nodes, fast advances 3 nodes
questions.explanation: The slow pointer advances 1 step while the fast pointer advances 2 steps. If a cycle exists, they are guaranteed to meet inside the loop.

questions.prompt: What is the in-order traversal of a valid Binary Search Tree (BST) guaranteed to produce?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits (Left, Root, Right), which in a BST outputs keys in strictly ascending sorted order.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm finds single-source shortest paths in a graph with non-negative edge weights in O((V + E) log V) time?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra’s algorithm using a priority queue/min-heap efficiently computes non-negative shortest paths in O((V+E) log V).

questions.prompt: What are the two foundational prerequisites for applying Dynamic Programming to an optimization problem?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Programming applies when a problem exhibits optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems that can be cached.
